title: Something Very Bad Is Gonna Happen
sourceTitle: Something Very Bad Is Gonna Happen
synopsis: You woke up at 4:11 a.m. with the deep, unshakable certainty that something very bad is about to happen — today, here, to someone you love. You have until the end of the day to figure out what, and whether you can stop it.

nodes.text: The feeling arrives before you're fully awake — heavy and certain, like furniture in a dark room. Something very bad is going to happen. You don't know what, only that it's today. The air in 4:11 a.m.

choices.text: Get up and write down everything you sense
choices.consequence: List the dread before it scatters. You get up and write down everything you sense. The way toward The List opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Try to go back to sleep — it's just a dream
choices.consequence: Denial is a curtain, not a door. You try to go back to sleep — it's just a dream. The way toward Coffee opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: On a notepad you write: kitchen, car, your sister, the stairs at work, the bridge. Even reading it back, your hand shakes. Some of these mean nothing. One of them is the thing. “Take the list seriously, item by item” draws you toward Your Sister Calls; “Burn the list and shake it off” leaves The Office waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Take the list seriously, item by item
choices.consequence: Superstition is sometimes pattern recognition. You choose to take the list seriously, item by item. By Your Sister Calls, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Burn the list and shake it off
choices.consequence: Naming a fear gives it shape. You commit to burn the list and shake it off. It carries you into The Office while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: By 7 a.m. you are pretending it's a normal day, with normal coffee. Your partner asks why you keep glancing at the door. You don't have a good answer. The feeling, in daylight, has not gotten smaller.

choices.text: Tell your partner the truth
choices.consequence: Saying it aloud is a kind of test. You choose to tell your partner the truth. By Your Sister Calls, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Keep it to yourself — they'll think you're spiraling
choices.consequence: Some weights are quieter alone. You commit to keep it to yourself — they'll think you're spiraling. It carries you into The Office while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: She calls at 7:42 about nothing — running late, the car making a sound, did you call Mom. You hear, very clearly, the thing on your list. The car. The sound. Today. Choose “Tell her not to drive, no matter what” and She Won't Listen comes into view; choose “Ask careful questions without alarming her” and the road bends toward The Pattern.

choices.text: Tell her not to drive, no matter what
choices.consequence: Sometimes love sounds like a command. You tell her not to drive, no matter what. The way toward She Won't Listen opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Ask careful questions without alarming her
choices.consequence: A net cast wider may catch more. You ask careful questions without alarming her. The way toward The Pattern opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: At work the stairwell looks longer than usual. The fluorescents tick. Your boss tells a story about a near-miss on the way in and you actually flinch — and notice that nobody else does. The distance between She Won't Listen and The Pattern begins with the choice between “Take the stairs anyway” and “Take the elevator and feel ridiculous.”

choices.text: Take the stairs anyway
choices.consequence: Confront what your gut accuses. You choose to take the stairs anyway. By She Won't Listen, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Take the elevator and feel ridiculous
choices.consequence: Some battles are not today's. You commit to take the elevator and feel ridiculous. It carries you into The Pattern while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your sister laughs — kindly. 'You're being weird,' she says. 'I love you. Bye.' She hangs up and you stand in your kitchen with the phone still warm, and the feeling thickens like fog. “Drive to her right now” draws you toward The Drive; “Trust her and turn your attention elsewhere” leaves The Quiet Warning waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Drive to her right now
choices.consequence: Your body knows what your reasons don't. You commit to drive to her right now. It carries you into The Drive while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Trust her and turn your attention elsewhere
choices.consequence: You can't be in every room. You trust her and turn your attention elsewhere. The way toward The Quiet Warning opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: On the second floor you notice things — a damp patch on the ceiling near the server room, a colleague rubbing her chest, your phone buzzing with an unknown caller. The feeling is sharpening into specifics, but slowly, and not in time.

choices.text: Pull the fire alarm to clear the building
choices.consequence: Disruption now beats catastrophe later. You pull the fire alarm to clear the building. The way toward The Drive opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Quietly tell your supervisor what you sense
choices.consequence: Authority lends courage to weird truths. You choose to quietly tell your supervisor what you sense. By The Quiet Warning, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You're in your car heading to your sister's office or your own, depending — and you realize you're going too fast, and your hands are very cold. The feeling now includes you. Maybe the thing is you.

choices.text: Pull over and breathe before continuing
choices.consequence: You can't save anyone from a wreck you caused. You pull over and breathe before continuing. The way toward 10:47 a.m. opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Keep going — the urgency is the message
choices.consequence: Hesitation has a body count too. You keep going — the urgency is the message. The way toward Your Mother Calls opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Your supervisor frowns and humors you — but she also calls maintenance and tells the floor to stay clear of the stairwell. Small actions ripple. Maybe that's all it takes. “Trust that small actions are enough” draws you toward 10:47 a.m.; “Push for a bigger response anyway” leaves Your Mother Calls waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Trust that small actions are enough
choices.consequence: Big disasters often arrive on small hinges. You commit to trust that small actions are enough. It carries you into 10:47 a.m. while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Push for a bigger response anyway
choices.consequence: Better foolish and safe than reasonable and sorry. You commit to push for a bigger response anyway. It carries you into Your Mother Calls while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: There is a sound — not big, not yet — somewhere across the city. A pop. A drop in air pressure. A siren two blocks over. The feeling now is a needle in your chest. “Run toward the sound to help” draws you toward Hospital Hallway; “Find your people first” leaves Lockdown waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Run toward the sound to help
choices.consequence: Compassion outruns dread, when it can. You run toward the sound to help. The way toward Hospital Hallway opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Find your people first
choices.consequence: You can't save the world without your own. You choose to find your people first. By Lockdown, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Mom: 'I had the strangest dream about you.' She is not psychic. She is, today, exactly as scared as you are. Until this moment you were maybe two thirds sure you weren't losing your mind.

choices.text: Tell her everything you've sensed
choices.consequence: Two witnesses make a fact. You commit to tell her everything you've sensed. It carries you into Hospital Hallway while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Lie to keep her calm
choices.consequence: Love and lying share a border. You commit to lie to keep her calm. It carries you into Lockdown while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Someone you love is here — your sister, your colleague, a stranger you couldn't reach — and the corridor smells like coffee and fear. The feeling has narrowed to one door and one held breath. Choose “Sit and wait for news” and The Small Good comes into view; choose “Demand information from someone in scrubs” and the road bends toward The News.

choices.text: Sit and wait for news
choices.consequence: Some battles are about endurance. You sit and wait for news. The way toward The Small Good opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Demand information from someone in scrubs
choices.consequence: Polite has a cost; impolite has a different one. You commit to demand information from someone in scrubs. It carries you into The News while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your phone fills with alerts and your office goes on lockdown for a reason nobody upstairs has named yet. People text 'are you ok' and you can only answer 'I think so.' The feeling shrinks slightly — and gets darker.

choices.text: Help organize the people around you
choices.consequence: Action is the antidote to dread. You choose to help organize the people around you. By The Small Good, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Call everyone you love, in order
choices.consequence: Make sure they hear your voice today. You commit to call everyone you love, in order. It carries you into The News while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: A nurse, a stranger, a child holds your hand for a moment. Whatever the catastrophe was or wasn't, the day is still full of small good people. The feeling does not lift. It just becomes survivable.

choices.text: Notice the goodness and let it steady you
choices.consequence: Beauty doesn't cancel dread; it carries it. You commit to notice the goodness and let it steady you. It carries you into Evening while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Keep scanning for the next danger
choices.consequence: Vigilance is hard to switch off. You commit to keep scanning for the next danger. It carries you into Aftershock while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The first reports are wrong, like they always are. Then the second reports are wrong differently. Eventually a true sentence arrives, and it is both better and worse than what your body told you at 4:11.

choices.text: Sit with the true sentence
choices.consequence: Truth is a posture you have to settle into. You choose to sit with the true sentence. By Evening, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Try to make sense of why you felt it
choices.consequence: Meaning is a balm and sometimes a trap. You choose to try to make sense of why you felt it. By Aftershock, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The day is winding down without ending you. Your sister is alive, or recovering, or grieving someone else; either way, she is on the other end of a phone call, breathing. You sit by a window and watch the city's lights come on.

choices.text: Decide the feeling was real and useful
choices.consequence: Believe your body next time, too. You commit to decide the feeling was real and useful. It carries you into 11:11 p.m. while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Decide it was coincidence with bad timing
choices.consequence: Skepticism is a kind of mercy on yourself. You commit to decide it was coincidence with bad timing. It carries you into What You'll Carry while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: A second wave hits — a smaller thing, a near-miss, a phone call about a different cousin. The feeling is now a familiar weight, no longer a stranger. You will, you realize, live the rest of your life with this voice.

choices.text: Make peace with the voice and listen carefully
choices.consequence: A reliable warning is a strange gift. You choose to make peace with the voice and listen carefully. By 11:11 p.m., the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Decide to fight the voice with therapy and routine
choices.consequence: You don't have to inherit your own dread forever. You commit to decide to fight the voice with therapy and routine. It carries you into What You'll Carry while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: An ordinary hour again. You light a candle for no reason and notice you didn't get killed today, and neither did the people you love most. That is not a small thing. That is, in fact, the only thing.

choices.text: Call your mother before bed
choices.consequence: The bad things will or won't come. Love now. You choose to call your mother before bed. By The Calls, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Write down what you learned today
choices.consequence: Memory is the only seatbelt against forgetting. You commit to write down what you learned today. It carries you into Going to Bed while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You won't tell most people about this day. You'll carry it like a small smooth stone in a pocket — a reminder that catastrophe was once close, and the city kept going, and so did you. It is, somehow, comforting.

choices.text: Keep the stone and the lesson
choices.consequence: Some weights are also anchors. You choose to keep the stone and the lesson. By The Calls, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Put the stone down and walk lighter
choices.consequence: You're allowed to forget on purpose. You put the stone down and walk lighter. The way toward Going to Bed opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You call them — sister, partner, mother, the friend you've been meaning to. Not big speeches. Just 'I love you, I'm glad you're here.' Some of them cry a little. Most of them say 'are you okay?' You are. You are.

choices.text: Make this your new ordinary
choices.consequence: Call the people now, before the next 4:11. You commit to make this your new ordinary. It carries you into Until the Next 4:11 while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Drift back to your old habits in a week
choices.consequence: Even good lessons need re-learning. You choose to drift back to your old habits in a week. By Ordinary, Mostly, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Sleep doesn't come fast. The feeling, just before you drift off, returns gently — but this time it's not a warning. It's the simple bedrock fact that you are mortal, and so is everyone you love, and tonight, again, nobody is gone.

choices.text: Sleep with the knowledge as a comfort
choices.consequence: Mortality is also permission to love now. You choose to sleep with the knowledge as a comfort. By Until the Next 4:11, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Sleep with one eye open from now on
choices.consequence: Vigilance can be a vow, not a curse. You choose to sleep with one eye open from now on. By The Watchful Heart, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You don't get more days than you got. You get to do something with the ones you have. The feeling becomes a quiet companion — not a fortune teller, not a curse — just the part of you that has noticed how lucky you are, and how briefly.

Time blunts the day. You forget some of the details and remember the rest wrong. That is okay. Most of being human is forgetting what almost killed you and showing up to dinner anyway. The road into Ordinary, Mostly began with “Drift back to your old habits in a week” in The Calls; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You become someone who picks up the phone fast, who locks the door, who checks the smoke detector twice. People tease you for it. People also, on the worst day of their lives, call you first. You are, in a way nobody planned, useful.
